lightDist.note: Full-sample raw composite centres for live display. Regenerated by npm run calibrate:lights. bake:history uses an expanding window so the archive has no look-ahead in the means; outputScale then equalizes pooled sds so ±0.45 is the same percentile in each light.

WALCL.name: Fed assets
WALCL.note: Fed's total balance-sheet assets. Rising = more liquidity into the system.

WRESBAL.name: Bank reserves at Fed
WRESBAL.note: Cash banks hold at the Fed. Falling reserves often mean tighter money-market conditions.

RRPONTSYD.name: Overnight reverse repo
RRPONTSYD.note: Overnight reverse repo — cash parked at the Fed. Drained to near zero since 2023, so the level no longer says much; the direction still does.

WTREGEN.name: Treasury cash account
WTREGEN.note: Treasury General Account — the government's Fed checking account. Rise pulls reserves out of banks.

WSHOSHO.name: Fed securities held
WSHOSHO.note: Securities the Fed holds outright (QE stock). Core of balance-sheet liquidity.

M2SL.name: US money supply (M2)
M2SL.note: Broad US money supply (cash, checking, savings). Slow growth can signal tight credit.

TOTLL.name: US bank loans & leases
TOTLL.note: Total bank loans & leases. Private credit still flowing to the real economy.

CHINA_CREDIT_GDP.name: China credit / GDP
CHINA_CREDIT_GDP.note: BIS total credit to China's private non-financial sector as a share of GDP (break-adjusted). The free 2003+ China credit stock — monthly TSF is not on FRED and the public MOFCOM feed only starts in 2015. Shown, not voted: it is a stock that ratchets, it has reached the top of its 2003-2026 band (111 / 169 / 194) and printed +1.00 every day, and BIS lags two to three quarters so the reading can be 13 months old. China reaches Liquidity through FX reserves in the G4 ballot. The four-quarter impulse is lagged with the stock — it does not vote a 1m turn.
CHINA_CREDIT_GDP.sub: BIS total credit to private non-financial

anchor.why: China credit 201% of GDP — 111 is the 2003–06 floor, 169 the median, 194 the post-2016 plateau

BUSLOANS.name: Business bank loans
BUSLOANS.note: H.8 weekly C&I loans (FRED TOTCI). FRED’s BUSLOANS ticker is monthly; this is the weekly print.

GFDEBTN.name: US federal debt
GFDEBTN.note: Total US federal debt outstanding. Stock of government paper, not the monthly deficit.

TRESEGCNM052N.name: China FX reserves
TRESEGCNM052N.note: China's foreign-exchange reserves. Proxy for Asia USD liquidity and China capital flows.

ECBASSETS.name: ECB assets
ECBASSETS.note: European Central Bank balance sheet. Euro-area QE/QT pulse.

JPNASSETS.name: Bank of Japan assets
JPNASSETS.note: Bank of Japan assets. Japan still a huge global liquidity source.

SOFR.name: SOFR overnight rate
SOFR.note: Secured Overnight Financing Rate — US overnight secured funding cost. Higher = tighter cash.

EFFR.name: Fed funds rate
EFFR.note: Effective Federal Funds Rate — where overnight bank reserves actually trade vs the Fed target.

CPFF.name: Commercial paper stress
CPFF.note: 90-day AA financial commercial paper minus the fed funds rate — what it costs a bank or a large company to roll unsecured short-term debt, over the policy rate. The price of funding rather than the quantity of reserves, which is why it stays honest in a crisis: 242bp at the October 2008 peak and 197bp in March 2020, against 22bp today. Daily from 1997, so it covers the whole 2003 archive. Band is the measured 2003-2026 distribution: 3bp is the 25th percentile, 21bp the 75th, 75bp roughly the 97th — normal variation reads neutral and only genuine stress reads tight.

anchor.why: commercial paper 19bp over fed funds — 21bp is typical, 242bp was October 2008

DFEDTAR.name: Fed funds target (legacy)
DFEDTAR.note: Single fed funds target through December 2008. Used only to build the pre-SOFR funding spread (EFFR − target); does not vote a component.

DGS3MO.name: US 3-month yield
DGS3MO.note: 3-month Treasury yield. Short-rate anchor near Fed policy.

DGS2.name: US 2-year yield
DGS2.note: 2-year Treasury yield. Highly sensitive to near-term Fed path.

anchor.why: trailing real short rate 1.74% (nominal 4.75 − core PCE 3.0)

DGS5.name: US 5-year yield
DGS5.note: 5-year Treasury yield. Mid-curve — mix of policy path and growth/inflation views.

DGS10.name: US 10-year yield
DGS10.note: 10-year Treasury yield. Benchmark long rate for mortgages, corporates, and risk assets.

DGS30.name: US 30-year yield
DGS30.note: 30-year Treasury yield. Ultra-long duration; sensitive to term premium and fiscal supply.

T10Y2Y.name: 2s10s curve
T10Y2Y.note: 10y minus 2y curve. Negative (inverted) often warns of slowdown; steepening can ease long-end conditions.

T10Y3M.name: 3m10s curve
T10Y3M.note: 10y minus 3m curve. Another recession-signal spread; deeper inversion = tighter credit impulse.

DFII5.name: 5-year real yield
DFII5.note: 5-year TIPS real yield — the market’s real funding rate. Votes Rates on the real-rate band; do not replace this with nominal minus trailing core PCE.

DFII10.name: 10-year real yield
DFII10.note: 10-year TIPS real yield — the discount rate risk assets actually face. Votes Rates on the real-rate band.

T5YIE.name: 5-year inflation bet
T5YIE.note: 5-year breakeven inflation — market's expected average CPI over 5 years.

T10YIE.name: 10-year inflation bet
T10YIE.note: 10-year breakeven inflation — market's long-run inflation pricing.

T5YIFR.name: 5y5y forward inflation
T5YIFR.note: 5y5y forward inflation — inflation expected 5–10 years out. The Fed's preferred long-run gauge, and Inflation's market voter: 2.3% is the CPI-equivalent of a 2% PCE target. Realized PCE and this print can disagree; when they do, Inflation says so.

anchor.why: 5y5y 2.3% — 2.3 is the CPI-equivalent of a 2% PCE target

DTWEXBGS.name: Broad US dollar index
DTWEXBGS.note: Fed broad dollar trade-weighted index. Stronger dollar = tighter USD liquidity abroad.

RBUSBIS.name: Real dollar index
RBUSBIS.note: BIS real effective USD — inflation-adjusted dollar strength vs trading partners.

IRLTLT01DEM156N.name: German 10-year yield
IRLTLT01DEM156N.note: German 10-year Bund yield, OECD monthly average. Slow official print; the live tape is Bund 10-year (Bundesbank daily).

IRLTLT01GBM156N.name: UK 10-year yield
IRLTLT01GBM156N.note: UK 10-year Gilt yield, OECD monthly average. Slow official print; the live tape is Gilt 10-year (BoE daily).

IRLTLT01JPM156N.name: Japan 10-year yield
IRLTLT01JPM156N.note: Japan 10-year JGB yield, OECD monthly average. Slow official print; the live tape is JGB 10-year (MOF daily).

DE10Y.name: Bund 10-year
DE10Y.note: Constant-maturity 10-year Bund yield from the Bundesbank term structure. Daily official print.

GB10Y.name: Gilt 10-year
GB10Y.note: Bank of England daily 10-year nominal par yield on gilts (IUDSNPY).

JP10Y.name: JGB 10-year
JP10Y.note: Japan Ministry of Finance daily 10-year JGB par yield.

MOVE.name: Bond volatility (MOVE)
MOVE.note: ICE BofA MOVE — implied vol on Treasuries. The rates complex’s stress gauge: a spike taxes Rates (dealers won’t warehouse duration); calm does not vote easy.

anchor.why: MOVE 101 — elevated, taxes the rates complex

DXY.name: Dollar index (DXY)
DXY.note: ICE US Dollar Index vs majors (EUR, JPY, GBP, CAD, SEK, CHF). Classic DXY tape.

EURUSD.name: Euro vs dollar
EURUSD.note: Euros per dollar. Higher = stronger euro / weaker dollar.

USDJPY.name: Dollar vs yen
USDJPY.note: Yen per dollar. Higher = stronger dollar vs yen (often risk-off or rate-gap driven).

USDCNH.name: Dollar vs yuan
USDCNH.note: Offshore yuan per dollar. Higher = weaker CNH; China/EM stress tell.

GBPUSD.name: Pound vs dollar
GBPUSD.note: Pounds per dollar. Higher = stronger sterling.

AUDUSD.name: Aussie vs dollar
AUDUSD.note: Aussie dollar vs USD. Risk/commodity-linked FX.

USDMXN.name: Dollar vs peso
USDMXN.note: Pesos per dollar. Higher = weaker peso; EM stress proxy.

STICKY_CPI.name: Sticky CPI
STICKY_CPI.note: Atlanta Fed sticky CPI, 12-month change. M157 is the month-ago print (~0.3%) and must not be scored as YoY.

INDPRO.name: Industrial production
INDPRO.note: US industrial production index. Factory and utility output pulse.

PAYEMS.name: Nonfarm payrolls
PAYEMS.note: Nonfarm payrolls — monthly jobs added. Headline labor-market print.

UNRATE.name: Unemployment rate
UNRATE.note: Unemployment rate. Rising = labor market cooling (soft for growth).

EA_UNRATE.name: Euro area unemployment
EA_UNRATE.note: Harmonized unemployment rate for the euro area. On the book, does not vote Growth.

JP_UNRATE.name: Japan unemployment
JP_UNRATE.note: Harmonized unemployment rate for Japan. On the book, does not vote Growth.

ICSA.name: Initial jobless claims
ICSA.note: Initial jobless claims — weekly new unemployment filings. Fast labor stress tell.

CCSA.name: Continuing claims
CCSA.note: Continuing claims — people still on unemployment. Stickier labor softening.

JTSJOL.name: Job openings
JTSJOL.note: JOLTS job openings, 12-month change. Leading labor demand (the stock of openings drifted up for a decade, so Growth reads YoY).

JTSQUR.name: Quit rate
JTSQUR.note: JOLTS quit rate. Workers' confidence quitting — high = tight labor market.

CES0500000003.name: Average hourly earnings
CES0500000003.note: Average hourly earnings, scored as 12-month %. Wage pressure into inflation and margins.

RSAFS.name: Retail sales
RSAFS.note: Advance retail sales. Consumer spending pulse (nominal).

DGORDER.name: Durable goods orders
DGORDER.note: Durable goods orders, 12-month change. Leading factory demand (dollar levels grow forever, so Growth reads YoY).

HOUST.name: Housing starts
HOUST.note: Housing starts — homes breaking ground. Leading growth sleeve.

PERMIT.name: Building permits
PERMIT.note: Building permits — forward housing demand. Leading growth sleeve.

CPIAUCSL.name: Headline CPI
CPIAUCSL.note: Headline CPI (all items). What households feel; noisy month to month.

CPILFESL.name: Core CPI
CPILFESL.note: Core CPI (ex food & energy). Fed's preferred CPI underlying read.

PCEPI.name: Headline PCE
PCEPI.note: Headline PCE price index — Fed's official inflation target basket.

PCEPILFE.name: Core PCE
PCEPILFE.note: Core PCE (ex food & energy). The Fed's main inflation target series.

MICH.name: Inflation expectations
MICH.note: UMich 1-year inflation expectations. Household inflation psychology — on the book and the lookback, does not vote Inflation. Households run hot versus the Fed's basket.

GDPC1.name: Real GDP
GDPC1.note: Real GDP YoY. Volume of the whole economy — the real side of growth.

GDP.name: Nominal GDP
GDP.note: Nominal GDP YoY. Dollar spending in the economy — growth + prices. Split vs real GDP tells you how much of the heat is real vs inflation.

COPPER.name: Copper
COPPER.note: Copper futures. "Dr. Copper" — industrial demand / global growth proxy.

VIX.name: Equity volatility (VIX)
VIX.note: Cboe VIX — 30-day implied vol on the S&P 500. Equity fear gauge.

BAMLH0A0HYM2.name: High-yield spread
BAMLH0A0HYM2.note: ICE BofA high-yield OAS. Extra yield high-yield bonds demand over Treasuries. FRED only publishes three years; the band is the long-run shape (2.5 tights / 4 typical / 6.5 stress), not this download. Baa over 10s is the long credit voter and carries more weight.

anchor.why: High-yield OAS 3.1% — 2.5 is cycle tights, 4 is typical, 6.5 is stress

BAMLC0A0CM.name: IG credit spread
BAMLC0A0CM.note: ICE BofA investment-grade OAS. Extra yield on investment-grade corporates — milder credit stress.

NFCI.name: Financial conditions
NFCI.note: Chicago Fed National Financial Conditions Index. Higher = tighter US financial conditions.

ANFCI.name: Adjusted financial cond.
ANFCI.note: Adjusted NFCI — strips out economic activity so it's more about pure financial stress.

SPX.name: S&P 500
SPX.note: S&P 500. Broad US large-cap equity risk appetite.

SPX_EY.name: S&P earnings yield
SPX_EY.note: S&P 500 trailing earnings yield (Multpl). Valuation input for Equities — compared with the 10y real yield as EQUITY_ERP.

XLY.name: Consumer disc. ETF
XLY.note: Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR. Coarse US cyclical equity proxy for the Equities split.

XLP.name: Consumer staples ETF
XLP.note: Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR. Coarse US defensive equity proxy for the Equities split.

NDX.name: Nasdaq 100
NDX.note: Nasdaq-100. US mega-cap / growth equity tape.

RTY.name: Russell 2000
RTY.note: Russell 2000. US small-cap risk — more domestic and credit-sensitive.

GOLD.name: Gold
GOLD.note: Gold futures. Real-rate / dollar / fear hedge — treat as an output, not a cause.

BTC.name: Bitcoin
BTC.note: Bitcoin. Speculative liquidity-sensitive risk asset — output, not input.

WTI.name: WTI crude oil
WTI.note: West Texas Intermediate crude. US oil benchmark.

MTSDS133FMS.name: Fed budget balance
MTSDS133FMS.note: Monthly federal budget balance. Deficit (−) means more Treasury issuance ahead.

ROW_UST.name: Foreign UST holdings
ROW_UST.note: Foreign holdings of US Treasuries. Soft = overseas buyers stepping back.

TREAST.name: Fed Treasury holdings
TREAST.note: Fed's SOMA Treasury holdings — the QE/QT Treasury piece of the balance sheet.

FYGFDPUN.name: Debt held by public
FYGFDPUN.note: Debt held by the public (ex Fed/gov accounts). The stock markets actually finance.

DFEDTARU.name: Fed funds target (top)
DFEDTARU.note: Top of the Fed's federal funds target range. Used to build SOFR_SPREAD; does not vote Rates — audit:bands flagged it pinned (~54%) as a near-constant after trailing-PCE deflation.

DFEDTARL.name: Fed funds target (low)
DFEDTARL.note: Bottom of the Fed's federal funds target range. Official policy rate floor.

MORTGAGE30US.name: 30-year mortgage rate
MORTGAGE30US.note: Average 30-year fixed mortgage rate. Direct hit to housing and consumer duration.

THREEFFTP10.name: 10y term premium
THREEFFTP10.note: NY Fed ACM 10y forward term premium — extra yield for long-bond risk, beyond rate-path expectations.

THREEFFTP2.name: 2y term premium
THREEFFTP2.note: NY Fed ACM 2y forward term premium — near-term bond risk premium.

T10YFF.name: 10y vs fed funds
T10YFF.note: 10y yield minus fed funds. Positive steepness vs policy; compressed = tighter/longer-end caution.

USDCHF.name: Dollar vs franc
USDCHF.note: Swiss francs per dollar. Higher = stronger USD / weaker CHF safe-haven bid fading.

USDCAD.name: Dollar vs loonie
USDCAD.note: Canadian dollars per dollar. Oil- and NAFTA-sensitive cross.

USDBRL.name: Dollar vs real
USDBRL.note: Reais per dollar. Higher = weaker BRL; EM stress proxy.

EURJPY.name: Euro vs yen
EURJPY.note: Euro vs yen. Classic risk-on cross — rises when risk appetite improves.

EMPIRE_MFG.name: Empire manufacturing
EMPIRE_MFG.note: NY Fed Empire State manufacturing survey. Regional PMI-style activity — Growth survey sleeve.

PHILLY_MFG.name: Philly manufacturing
PHILLY_MFG.note: Philly Fed manufacturing survey. Regional PMI-style activity — Growth survey sleeve.

CFNAI.name: Chicago Fed activity
CFNAI.note: Chicago Fed National Activity Index. Broad monthly growth factor (0 ≈ trend).

WEI.name: Weekly economic index
WEI.note: NY Fed Weekly Economic Index. High-frequency real activity blend.

CSUSHPISA.name: Case-Shiller home prices
CSUSHPISA.note: Case-Shiller home price index. National house-price level.

EXHOSLUSM495S.name: Existing home sales
EXHOSLUSM495S.note: Existing home sales. Housing turnover — rates and affordability.

UMCSENT.name: Consumer sentiment
UMCSENT.note: University of Michigan consumer sentiment. Soft demand / mood gauge.

PPIACO.name: Commodity PPI
PPIACO.note: PPI all commodities. Upstream goods inflation.

PPIFIS.name: Final-demand PPI
PPIFIS.note: PPI final demand. Pipeline prices into consumer inflation.

MEDIAN_CPI.name: Median CPI
MEDIAN_CPI.note: Cleveland Fed median CPI. Robust underlying inflation (less noisy than mean).

TRIMMED_CPI.name: Trimmed-mean CPI
TRIMMED_CPI.note: Cleveland Fed trimmed-mean CPI. Another core-like inflation measure.

SHELTER_CPI.name: CPI shelter
SHELTER_CPI.note: CPI shelter. Housing rents/OER — big, sticky CPI weight.

SUPERCORE.name: Services CPI ex energy
SUPERCORE.note: CPI services ex energy. "Supercore" — services inflation the Fed watches.

CORESTICK.name: Sticky core CPI
CORESTICK.note: Atlanta Fed sticky core CPI. Core prices that are slow to change.

EA_HICP.name: Euro area HICP
EA_HICP.note: Euro area HICP all-items, 12-month change. On the book, does not vote Inflation. Eurostat's old annual-rate series ended with 2025; this is the live index.

BAA10Y.name: Baa spread over 10s
BAA10Y.note: Moody's Baa corporate yield minus the 10-year Treasury - the extra yield demanded to lend to a middling company. Widening means doubt that borrowers pay. FRED computes this one rather than licensing it, so it carries 40 years of history and can be scored consistently across past cycles: 2.1 is the long-run median, 3.3 is where 2011 and 2016 topped out, and the 2008 peak was 6.07.

anchor.why: Baa over 10s 1.48pp — 2.1 is the 40-year median, 3.3 is crisis

BBB_OAS.name: BBB credit spread
BBB_OAS.note: ICE BofA BBB option-adjusted spread. FRED's open download only carries about three years, and that whole window sits at cycle tights near 1% — so a print of 1.00 is the market, not a stuck feed. Risk votes Moody's Baa over 10s (1986+) instead. Sanity still range-checks this series.

HY_CCC_OAS.name: CCC credit spread
HY_CCC_OAS.note: CCC high-yield OAS. Distressed credit; blows out in risk-off. FRED only ships about three years. The long record ran from 4.14 (June 2007) to 44.29 (December 2008); the sanity ceiling is that range, not this download.

EPU.name: Policy uncertainty
EPU.note: Economic Policy Uncertainty index. News-based US policy risk.

SAHM.name: Sahm recession rule
SAHM.note: Sahm rule trigger — unemployment jump vs recent low. Recession flag when ≥0.5.

HYG.name: High-yield bond ETF
HYG.note: iShares High Yield Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for high-yield credit (up = easier).

LQD.name: IG bond ETF
LQD.note: iShares Investment Grade Corporate Bond ETF. Price tape for investment-grade credit.

SKEW.name: Crash-insurance skew
SKEW.note: Cboe SKEW — price of S&P crash insurance (tail risk). Higher = more fear of a crash.

SILVER.name: Silver
SILVER.note: Silver futures. Precious metal with industrial demand too.

TLT.name: Long Treasury ETF
TLT.note: iShares 20+ Year Treasury ETF. Long-bond price tape (up = yields down).

EWZ.name: Brazil equity ETF
EWZ.note: iShares MSCI Brazil ETF. EM equity risk proxy.

EFA.name: Developed ex-US equities
EFA.note: iShares MSCI EAFE. Developed equities outside the US.

FEZ.name: Euro Stoxx 50 ETF
FEZ.note: SPDR Euro Stoxx 50. Core European equity risk.

EWJ.name: Japan equities
EWJ.note: iShares MSCI Japan. Japanese equity risk appetite.

EEM.name: Emerging market equities
EEM.note: iShares MSCI Emerging Markets. Broad EM equity risk.

FXI.name: China large-cap equities
FXI.note: iShares China Large-Cap. China equity risk proxy.

JNK.name: High-yield bond ETF
JNK.note: SPDR Bloomberg High Yield Bond ETF. Credit risk as a traded price.

IEF.name: 7–10y Treasury ETF
IEF.note: iShares 7–10 Year Treasury. Intermediate duration prices.

SHY.name: 1–3y Treasury ETF
SHY.note: iShares 1–3 Year Treasury. Short duration / cash-like rates.

TIP.name: TIPS ETF
TIP.note: iShares TIPS Bond ETF. Real-rate / inflation-protected duration.

NATGAS.name: Natural gas
NATGAS.note: Natural gas futures. Energy tape beyond oil.

ETH.name: Ethereum
ETH.note: Ethereum. Second crypto liquidity/risk proxy beside Bitcoin.

DJI.name: Dow Jones
DJI.note: Dow Jones Industrial Average. 30-name household US equity tape — narrower than the S&P 500.

EWY.name: Korea equities
EWY.note: iShares MSCI South Korea. Chip-cycle / export-growth equity tape.

INDA.name: India equities
INDA.note: iShares MSCI India. Large EM weight that was missing from the country set.

EMB.name: EM dollar bonds
EMB.note: iShares J.P. Morgan USD Emerging Markets Bond. EM credit as a traded price.

AGG.name: US aggregate bond ETF
AGG.note: iShares Core US Aggregate Bond. The whole investment-grade US bond market in one price.

PALL.name: Palladium
PALL.note: Palladium futures. Auto-catalyst metal — completes the precious/industrial set.

GASOLINE.name: RBOB gasoline
GASOLINE.note: RBOB gasoline futures. Downstream oil — the pump-price tape.

HEATOIL.name: Heating oil
HEATOIL.note: NYMEX heating oil / ULSD. Distillate — freight, heating, and the crack vs crude.

TTF.name: Dutch TTF gas
TTF.note: Dutch TTF natural gas. European gas benchmark — the non-US energy shock tape.

CORN.name: Corn
CORN.note: Corn futures. Global feed and ethanol grain.

WHEAT.name: Wheat
WHEAT.note: Chicago SRW wheat. Global food-grain tape.

SOY.name: Soybeans
SOY.note: Soybean futures. Protein / crush — China demand tell.

XRP.name: XRP
XRP.note: XRP. Cross-border payments crypto — beta to risk and regulation.

SOL.name: Solana
SOL.note: Solana. High-throughput smart-contract chain — crypto risk appetite.

TRX.name: TRON
TRX.note: TRON. High-volume settlement chain; often tracks crypto liquidity.

HYPE.name: Hyperliquid
HYPE.note: Hyperliquid. On-chain perp-DEX token — crypto trading-activity proxy.

DOGE.name: Dogecoin
DOGE.note: Dogecoin. Meme-beta crypto — retail risk appetite.

LEO.name: UNUS SED LEO
LEO.note: Bitfinex LEO. Exchange-utility token in the large-cap set.

LINK.name: Chainlink
LINK.note: Chainlink. Oracle infrastructure — DeFi plumbing tape.

LTC.name: Litecoin
LTC.note: Litecoin. Classic large-cap crypto beside Bitcoin.

NET_LIQ.name: Net liquidity
NET_LIQ.note: Street shorthand: Fed assets − TGA − ON RRP. Rising = more cash in markets.

SOFR_SPREAD.name: Funding vs target top
SOFR_SPREAD.note: Overnight funding minus the top of the fed funds target, in bp. From 2018-04-02 that is SOFR; before then EFFR versus DFEDTAR / DFEDTARU on the same band so the funding ballot covers the full archive. Deeply negative means reserves are so ample that cash trades well inside the corridor; at or above zero means reserves are scarce — that is where repo broke in September 2019. Reads reserve abundance, which is not the same as easy funding: in a crisis the Fed floods reserves *because* funding broke, so this print goes deeply negative at the worst moment. CPFF is the ballot that catches that.

anchor.why: funding -13bp vs the policy ceiling — above normal (5y average -17bp, +0.7σ); above normal means cash is getting scarce

RESERVES_GDP.name: Reserves ÷ GDP
RESERVES_GDP.note: Bank reserves measured against the size of the economy. The dollar figure always looks enormous, so the ratio is what tells you whether cash is genuinely ample: 6.9% when repo seized up in 2019, 16.6% at the QE peak.
RESERVES_GDP.sub: Bank reserves as share of GDP

anchor.why: reserves 9.3% of GDP — below normal for this system (5y average 11.5%, -1.2σ)

NETLIQ_GDP.name: Net liquidity ÷ GDP
NETLIQ_GDP.note: Fed assets minus the Treasury account minus reverse repo, measured against nominal GDP. Same idea as reserves over GDP but counts the whole plumbing stack: 16.6% before the 2019 squeeze, 27.8% at the QE peak.
NETLIQ_GDP.sub: Net liquidity as share of GDP

anchor.why: net liquidity 18.0% of GDP — below normal for this system (5y average 21.1%, -1.2σ)

GLOBAL_CB.name: G4 central bank assets
GLOBAL_CB.note: The four balance sheets that actually set the price of global money, converted to dollars at market rates so they can be added up. The China leg is FX reserves rather than the PBoC balance sheet, which FRED does not carry — for global dollar liquidity that is arguably the more relevant number, since it is the part that recycles into world markets.
GLOBAL_CB.sub: Fed + ECB + BoJ + PBoC, in dollars
GLOBAL_CB.source: derived (Fed + ECB + BoJ + China FX reserves, in USD)

GLOBAL_CB_YOY.name: Global CB assets, 12m
GLOBAL_CB_YOY.note: Year-over-year change in the G4 balance sheet in dollars. The level of a balance sheet grows forever and cannot carry a band; the rate of change is the thing that eases or tightens. Positive means the big four are net adding, negative means draining.
GLOBAL_CB_YOY.sub: Are the big four adding or draining?

anchor.why: G4 balance sheets -4.0% over 12m — flat is a mild drain, since world nominal GDP grows ~5%

DOLLAR_YOY.name: Dollar, 12m change
DOLLAR_YOY.note: Most of the world borrows in dollars it does not print. A rising dollar tightens every one of those balance sheets at once, regardless of what the Fed is doing, which is why it belongs in Liquidity and not just on the tape.

anchor.why: broad dollar +0.8% over 12m — a rising dollar tightens every borrower who owes in it

G3_10Y.name: Global long rates (G3)
G3_10Y.note: Average 10-year across Germany, the UK and Japan from official daily prints: Bundesbank Bund term structure, Bank of England gilt par yield, Japan MOF JGB. Duration is priced globally — when Bunds and JGBs move, Treasuries follow.
G3_10Y.sub: Mean of daily Bund, gilt and JGB 10-year
G3_10Y.source: derived (mean of daily Bund, gilt and JGB 10-year)

STOCK_BOND_CORR.name: Stock–bond correlation
STOCK_BOND_CORR.note: 60-day correlation of stocks vs bonds (sign-flipped). Rising together = less diversification.

CREDIT_IMPULSE.name: Credit impulse
CREDIT_IMPULSE.note: Change in the YoY growth rate of bank loans (TOTLL). Rising = credit accelerating into the economy — the private-sector impulse, not just Fed plumbing.

CHINA_CREDIT_IMPULSE.name: China credit impulse
CHINA_CREDIT_IMPULSE.note: Four-quarter change in China credit/GDP (pp of GDP). BIS-style impulse — free history to the mid-1980s. Monthly TSF impulse deferred until a free 2003+ flow series appears. Shown on the street; too lagged to vote a 1m turn.

NOM_REAL_SPREAD.name: Nominal − real GDP
NOM_REAL_SPREAD.note: Nominal GDP YoY minus real GDP YoY. Wide = more of the expansion is prices; tight = more is real activity. Core for credit vs duration attribution.

EQUITY_ERP.name: Equity risk premium
EQUITY_ERP.note: S&P earnings yield minus DFII10. Wide = equities cheap vs real duration; tight = not paid for equity risk.

GOLD_COT.name: Gold positioning
GOLD_COT.note: 156-week COT index of CFTC gold futures non-commercial net as a share of open interest. Crowded speculative longs tax the Gold box (rich positioning). Does not vote Risk. Raw contract counts drift with open interest, so the index is what carries the band.
GOLD_COT.source: derived (CFTC gold NC % OI, 156w COT index via FuturesBench)

anchor.why: gold speculative positioning 86 (156w index) — 93 is crowded long (p90)

formula.lights: Regime components = weighted mean of voter anchors (related series share a group first). Flow series can move the chevron only. 1w/2w/1m = impulse only. Score >+0.45 / <−0.45 paints the reading. Inflation upside = hot vs ~2%.

BAMLH0A0HYM2.why: ICE HY OAS on FRED is ~3y of cycle tights (archive median ~3.05). Centre sits at 3.5 — between that sample and the long-run typical of 4 — so the valuation leg still separates days inside this regime without treating cycle-tights as normal.
